intro_p: Serracapriola is just a few kilometres from the Adriatic Sea and in a privileged position relative to the beaches of the Gargano. In about 15–20 minutes by car you can reach the first Adriatic beaches, while in an hour you reach the famous beaches of the Gargano promontory.
beach_marina_desc: The beach of Marina di Serracapriola is the closest seaside resort to the village. A sandy beach on the Adriatic, quiet and authentic, with clean water and little crowding. Ideal for a relaxing family day at the sea, away from the chaos of more touristy destinations.
beach_termoli_desc: Termoli is one of the most beautiful seaside resorts on the Molise coast, just a few kilometres from Serracapriola. Wide sandy beaches, crystal-clear waters, a delightful medieval historic centre and the port from which ferries depart for the Tremiti Islands.
beach_lesina_desc: One of the closest beaches to Serracapriola. Lesina is a picturesque village on the eponymous lake, but its marina faces directly onto the Adriatic with a long sandy beach, clear waters and full beach services. Ideal for families with children thanks to the shallow water and very fine sand.
beach_chieuti_desc: The municipality of Chieuti has a small marina with a free beach. Less equipped but wilder and quieter, ideal for those who love the sea in peace, away from the crowds.
beach_sanmenaio_desc: On the northern slopes of the Gargano, San Menaio is one of the most visited seaside resorts in the Foggia province. Long white sandy beaches, crystal-clear waters, Mediterranean pines reaching the sea. The San Menaio Pine Forest is a scene of rare beauty.
beach_rodi_desc: One of the most picturesque villages of the Gargano, Rodi is famous for its terraced lemon groves overlooking the sea and the intensely blue waters. Boats depart from here to the Tremiti Islands. The surrounding beaches alternate rocky coves with sandy stretches.
beach_tremiti_desc: The Tremiti archipelago, a UNESCO Heritage Site, is one of the most beautiful destinations in the Mediterranean. Transparent waters, rich seabeds, white limestone cliffs and fragrant Mediterranean vegetation. Reachable by ferry from Termoli, Vieste or Rodi Garganico. An unmissable trip if you are staying in the area.
beach_lagol_desc: Technically not the sea, but Lake Lesina — one of the largest coastal lagoons in Italy — offers a fascinating and unique lakeside landscape. The lake waters, separated from the Adriatic by a thin strip of sand, are rich in eels and other freshwater fish. Beautiful for boat trips and observing aquatic wildlife.
li_c1: June to September for the sea. July and August are the warmest and busiest months.
li_c2: Among the cleanest in Italy; many Gargano beaches have been awarded the Blue Flag.
li_c3: In the restaurants of Lesina Marina and the Gargano villages you can eat the freshest fish and seafood at reasonable prices.
li_c4: In the low season there are many free spaces; in August it is advisable to arrive early in the morning.
li_c5: The Gargano waters are ideal for diving: rocky seabeds, underwater caves and colourful fish.
